title: Constraint made cheaper than no constraint
subtitle: A grammar-bounded CUDA decoder in which enforcing the tool catalog costs less than not enforcing it

stats.label: less per token with the catalog enforced than with no constraint at all
trie nodes for 42 tools, held in 64 KiB of constant memory
bit-identity gates; identical top results across 2,345 shuffled batches

lede: Constrained decoding is usually a tax. A serving framework computes every logit, then masks the ones the grammar forbids, then samples. My tool-discovery decoder turns that around. The grammar knows, before a token's forward pass finishes, that the answer is one of the current node's outgoing edges, so the output layer only computes those. Around that idea is a decoder I built from the ground up in CUDA: a trie in constant memory, a device-resident decode loop, a batched engine with paged memory, and determinism by construction.
quote: Nothing is kept until it moves the 469-query wall clock.
evidence: Grammar-constrained decoding: a CUDA decoder whose output layer computes only the edges the trie permits, 172 µs less per token with the catalog enforced than with no constraint.
CUDA kernel development: a token trie of 607 nodes for 42 tools held in 64 KiB of constant memory, with masked sampling in one block of 256 threads.
Deterministic GPU computation: 12 of 12 bit-identity gates and identical top results across 2,345 shuffled batches.
Fail-loud inference design: a decoder that stops with an error when the mask leaves nothing, so a broken grammar never produces a plausible answer.
author: Corey James
